γράφος /ˈɣɾa.fos/ noun a written record, a letter; from γράφω, to write.

graphos

A multi-tenant property-graph service: PostgreSQL + Apache AGE behind a typed HTTP API.

For teams whose services share connected data (dependencies, assets, knowledge graphs, agent memory) and who already run PostgreSQL.

Your services and AI agents call one HTTP API; only graphos holds a connection to the database.

Get started Benchmarks GitHub

Open source · Apache-2.0 · version 0.15.0

pomentum/graphos

In 30 seconds

  • The problem: Connected data turns up in most systems. Once several services need it, each one ends up holding database credentials, writing its own Cypher, and solving bulk loading, indexing and isolation on its own.
  • The approach: One service owns the graph. Your services call a typed REST API, and AI agents use the same reads over MCP. Only graphos talks to PostgreSQL + Apache AGE, on a private network.
  • What it is not: Not a new database engine, and not tied to any domain: graphos ships no labels of its own. Not a Cypher passthrough either: Cypher is read-only, by design, because writing through the API is far faster and safer on AGE (why).
  • Licence: Apache-2.0. Optional community detection uses a GPL library, left out of the published images (details).

03 · FeaturesWhat sets it apart

Tenants and schema

Each tenant is its own AGE graph, and a caller reaches only the tenants it is granted. graphos ships no labels of its own: you declare yours, add property rules if you want them, and rename or deprecate them later, in place (usage).

Fast, idempotent writes

Send batches, an NDJSON stream or a whole snapshot. graphos stages them with COPY and upserts them, so sending the same data twice changes nothing: 1,153–4,840 edges a second in our benchmark, where per-row Cypher MERGE managed 31 (usage, AGE notes).

Reconcile by difference

Send the full set of a node's (or a type's) edges as your source has them. graphos adds, changes and removes only what differs, in one transaction (usage).

Graph algorithms

Communities (Louvain or Leiden, an optional extra), PageRank, betweenness, components and degree, computed beside the API and stored on the nodes. A re-run writes only what changed, and a community keeps its id from run to run (what each finds).

AI agents (MCP)

/mcp gives agents graphos's reads as tools, with the caller's own grants and a schema summary written for models. MCP clients sign people in by themselves (agents guide).

Change feed

Every write is recorded in the same transaction that makes it. Read the changes after a cursor, or follow them live (usage).

Everything else, from CSV import and rule-derived edges to background jobs, metrics and the audit log, is in the feature survey.

07 · Get startedRun it on your machine

Docker with a recent Docker Compose (the docker compose plugin) and about 4 GB of memory for Docker. These commands run the published images (ghcr.io/pomentum/graphos-api and graphos-ui, amd64 and arm64), so nothing is built. They leave out community detection, whose library is GPL: add -f docker-compose.igraph.yml to download it at the first start. To build from source, add -f docker-compose.build.yml (the installation guide).

git clone https://github.com/pomentum/graphos.git && cd graphos

# 1. Random database passwords and graphos's master key, written once to
#    services/graphos/deploy/secrets/ (gitignored)
bash scripts/init-secrets.sh            # Windows: pwsh scripts/init-secrets.ps1

# 2. Database, API and web UI, from the published images (leave out --profile ui for the API alone)
docker compose -f docker-compose.graphos.yml --profile ui up -d

# 3. Up?
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/readyz    # {"status":"ready",...}
  1. Sign in to the UI at http://127.0.0.1:8081 as graphos / graphos and choose a new password: the installation guide.
  2. Register a tenant, write nodes and edges, read them back: the usage guide, or the Python client (pip install graphos-client, on PyPI).
  3. Load the demo tenant to explore: 08_demo_ecosystem.py. Its communities, the colours of UI 01, need the igraph extra: start the stack with -f docker-compose.igraph.yml, or the demo loads without them.

08 · FAQQuestions people ask

Who is graphos for?

Teams with several services that share connected data, such as dependencies, assets, a knowledge graph or an agent's memory, and who run PostgreSQL or are happy to. If a single application owns the graph and needs to write it with Cypher, plain Apache AGE or a native graph database suits it better.

Why not Neo4j, or plain Apache AGE?

graphos runs on PostgreSQL, a database you may already operate, back up and monitor. It is Apache-2.0 (its optional community detection uses a GPL library, which installs have it), has tenants, users and grants built in, and keeps your data in AGE's own format, so you can leave at any time. Plain AGE gives you Cypher on PostgreSQL, but leaves every service to hold database credentials and to solve loading, indexing and isolation itself, with Cypher writes at about 31 edges a second.

A native graph database wins where you need deep, variable-length traversals (graphos expands up to 5 hops, finds paths of up to 8, and its console refuses variable-length patterns) or a workload that writes heavily in Cypher.

What is the licence, and where does GPL come in?

graphos and its published images are Apache-2.0, with permissively licensed dependencies only; the graph metrics (PageRank, betweenness, components and degree) run on rustworkx, which is Apache-2.0 as well. Community detection (Louvain and Leiden) needs python-igraph, which is GPL-2.0-or-later, so it is an optional extra. The published images leave it out; start them with -f docker-compose.igraph.yml and the container downloads it at its first start. A build from source includes it unless you set GRAPHOS_EXTRAS empty when you build (details).

Why is Cypher read-only?

Two reasons, both measured. Speed: per-row Cypher MERGE managed 31 edges a second, where graphos's COPY-staged upserts manage 1,153–4,840. Safety: AGE mishandles Cypher writes to tables carrying the columns graphos adds for revisions and communities (on AGE 1.6, they crashed the database server). Writing through the API also keeps revisions, the change feed and the audit log right. The console still reads with Cypher; it refuses write clauses before they reach the database (why every write is SQL).

How big can a tenant get?

graphos sets no limit on a tenant's size. What has been measured: a 251,246-node, 940,144-edge graph read on a laptop (above), the graph algorithms on synthetic graphs of up to 3.0 million edges, and the label map on ten million edges. A single snapshot import takes up to 50 million rows. Larger graphs mostly need more memory for PostgreSQL (tuning).

Can I leave?

Yes, at any time. Every tenant is an ordinary AGE graph in ordinary PostgreSQL tables: AGE's Cypher and plain SQL read it with no graphos running, and a dataset export loads into plain AGE. The guide Reading graphos's data without graphos shows how.

Is it ready for production?

It has what running it for other people needs: users, grants and single sign-on, secrets sealed at rest, statement timeouts, metrics and an audit log. Every change to main is tested in CI against PostgreSQL 18 with AGE 1.8, and an upgrade brings the database up to date when graphos starts. The HTTP API is versioned (/v1) and its contract is published as OpenAPI. graphos is still before 1.0, so a release can change the API; each release's changes are in the changelog.

Why do tokens last only 15 minutes?

So a leaked token is useful for minutes, not months. People and programs sign in once; the web UI and the Python client renew their tokens by themselves, so you rarely notice. The lifetime is a setting, GRAPHOS_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_S.
